note: From the 2026-08-03 research pass. Leads failed only our evidence bar or the count; blocked can never ship.

leads.name: Milestone Hackberry of the Todai-ji West Gate
leads.why: 3.95m girth and 30m, the tallest tree in the official Nara Park giant-tree course, believed to mark the milestone on the Kyoto road that begins at Todai-ji's Tegai-mon. Age explicitly not recorded, single official source, and no coordinate exists for the West Gate ruins in any gazetteer. Needs a pin before it can ship.

leads.name: Roben-sugi at Nigatsu-do
leads.why: Superb legend: the infant Roben was said to have been carried off by an eagle and left in its branches, and Todai-ji's founding abbot was reunited with his mother beneath it. But the original fell to a typhoon in 1961 and the present tree is a successor, roughly 60 years old. Includable only on the Kyoto Gion-cherry precedent, and only if the entry says plainly it is a replanting. Good open photos exist.

leads.name: Wakamiya Great Camphor, Kasuga Taisha
leads.why: Legend says Empress Jingu planted it. Sources contradict badly on size: 12.46m girth and 24m in one record against '8m+, 7m tall, three trees planted together' in another, which is not a rounding difference. No official register lists it, and the one open photo fails the card crop with stone lanterns filling the centre.

leads.name: Great Zelkova of Kasuga
leads.why: 4.9m girth, the largest zelkova in Nara Park, hollow and mossy. Single-sourced to the shrine's own forest-walk page, no coordinate, no age, and 'upper portions lost' needs checking that it is thriving rather than a relic.

leads.name: Cycad of Jokyo-ji
leads.why: Nara City Natural Monument, 1979, and close to the station. Small tree at a minor temple, thin sourcing, visitor access unverified.

leads.name: Bayberry of Oryu-ji
leads.why: Nara City Natural Monument, 1979. Same profile as the cycad: real designation, thin sourcing, access unverified.

leads.name: Persimmon of Jigen-ji
leads.why: Nara City Natural Monument, 1983. Real designation, thin sourcing, access unverified.

leads.name: Ichiigashi of the Kasugayama primeval forest
leads.why: 6.00m girth and 35m on the southern path, which would be a strong entry, but one source and no coordinate. A single named tree inside the forest can qualify even though the forest cannot.

leads.name: Yogo-no-Matsu, Kasuga Taisha
leads.why: NEVER SHIP. The original pine died in 1995; a successor sapling grows beside the surviving stump. Famous as the claimed origin of the pine painted on every Noh stage, though even that attribution is disputed as a later invention.

leads.name: Chisokuin Nara-no-Yaezakura
leads.why: NEVER SHIP. The tree designated a national Natural Monument in 1923 has died; today's cherries are propagated descendants. Chisokuin is a closed sub-temple open roughly one day a year.

leads.name: Kasugayama Primeval Forest
leads.why: NEVER SHIP as one entry. A Special Natural Monument covering a whole mountain, with no single tree and nowhere to stand. A named individual inside it can qualify separately.

leads.name: Kasuga Ichiigashi giant-tree group
leads.why: NEVER SHIP. Thirty-plus separate trees over 3m girth scattered across the precinct, designated as a group. No single destination.

leads.name: Sunazuri-no-Fuji
leads.why: NEVER SHIP. A wisteria vine on a trellis.

leads.name: Shoryaku-ji Kojii grove
leads.why: NEVER SHIP. A prefecturally designated grove rather than one tree, and Bodaisen-cho is well beyond the day-trip boundary.

leads.name: Takiyama left-spiral Torreya
leads.why: NEVER SHIP for Nara. A prefectural Natural Monument, but in Tsuge-Hayama-cho, inside the municipal boundary only through a merger and far over 30 minutes out.

leads.name: Tsukigase Oyama ancient plums
leads.blocked_reason: out of range, and an ensemble
leads.why: NEVER SHIP for Nara. City-designated in March 2026, but Tsukigase is roughly an hour out, and it is a group rather than one tree.

leads.name: The thousand-year cedar at the Kasuga Treasure Hall cafe
leads.why: NEVER SHIP. A cut stump on indoor display. Easy to confuse with the living great cedar, which is why it is recorded here.
